description: The Smart-Grid ICT Resilience Framework, published by KIT-SDQ, provides software for analysing information and communication components of a smart grid. The project belongs to Helmholtz research on critical-infrastructure resilience. Its user guide describes topology initialisation, impact analysis and attacker simulation. Inputs include an initialisation map, topology, scenario state, power specifications and assigned power. The commands return ICT elements, topology and scenario state, followed by modified power specifications and dysfunctional smart components. Coverage is a user-defined network; the README does not establish a geographic study area, observation period or fixed temporal resolution. Public source is available on GitHub under EPL-2.0, free of charge. Deployment uses Eclipse Modeling Tools, Sirius and MDSDProfiles, with RMI and command-line interfaces. The documented Eclipse version is 2019-09. Important limitations are an external couplingSG submodule for which access is required and tests that the README says are disabled. The software was not built or run in this review. It supports investigation of coupled electricity and ICT failures. As a catalogue comparison, it complements the general co-simulation role of HELICS (platform-helics); interoperability between them was not established.
